h: Cranes, canoes and Sir Peter Scott's old window
p: Slimbridge has a few tricks up its sleeve that you might not expect. Common cranes, tall elegant birds that had vanished from much of Britain, have been reintroduced to the Somerset Levels and beyond through a project that the reserve played a big part in, and you may spot them stalking the wet fields. The flamingos are a big hit too, with several kinds kept here, and they are noisy, pink and endlessly entertaining for little ones.

In the warmer months, keep an eye out for the guided canoe safaris and other seasonal experiences, which take you out on the water through reed-lined channels at duck's-eye level. They tend to be popular, so it's worth looking at what's on before you travel rather than banking on getting a space on the day.

Founder Sir Peter Scott lived here, and his house overlooks the water where he used to watch and paint the wild swans. He famously realised every Bewick's swan has its own unique bill pattern, and the study of those swans has carried on at Slimbridge for decades. It's a lovely bit of history to share with older children while you're watching the flocks.

Budget a full day if you can, and wear proper footwear because the site is large. Nearby, the village of Frampton on Severn has one of the longest village greens you'll ever see, the Gloucester and Sharpness Canal runs close by for towpath walks, and in Berkeley you'll find Dr Jenner's House, home of the pioneer of vaccination. Gloucester's cathedral and docks are a short drive north if you've still got energy left.
